item.title: Re: Succinct
item.content:encoded:
A combination of the first two, I think. The pacemaker knew its job was to keep the "mass of flesh" in working order, even if it couldn't make that make sense to the surgeon, but I think it also liked the mass; I have the sense that, as the surgeon brings life to the objects, they have a history that comes alive with them, and for the pacemaker, it would have gotten close to the mass, and wanted the best for it, beyond just a simple sense of duty.

And yes, the surgeon is very uncomfortable discussing his nature, and everyone brings up the damn eyes.

item.title: Succinct
item.content:encoded:
The SCP being uncomfortable discussing its age is a tiny detail that adds so much depth. I got the sense that he had a deep, unresolved conflict about his human nature vs the focus of his practice and was maybe in denial. It came off much more elegantly than if it had been addressed in the interview.

The pacemaker was intriguing. Was is sentimentality? Duty? Did it just not know how else to live?

item.content:encoded: I think one of the key factors in making this a good SCP is that at no time did I feel like I should identify with or be amazed by the subject. They don't even classify him as a person, they say he "appears" to be a person. It never really feels like there's a human being behind that mask, just some weird parody of a surgeon going through the motions in an impossible way.
